final.label: test-exists-and-reaches-changed-path

skill_entry.name: 14. A changed path needs a test that enters it from the production side
skill_entry.trigger: Any one of four. (a) New primitive: a new header under h/ declares a type with mutable state sized by a constant (an advancing index or count plus an array or ring), a Note or doc comment states an ordering, capacity, full, empty or exactly-once invariant, and `git grep -l -w <name> HEAD -- t/` is empty. (b) Orchestration bypass: a changed or added function F in h/ or src/ sits on the call chain from a production caller down to a function the diff added; F and its callers up to three levels have no t/ hit; every t/ hit on the chain is a callee below F; F's own added or removed lines contain a branch or loop. (c) Formula mirror: a hunk in h/ or src/ changes the right-hand side of an assignment to a dotted or arrow field, and a t/ file the diff does not touch assigns the same field. (d) Accessor swap: a test hunk replaces a resource acquisition with a different named member or function, and no comment, commit message or body sentence names the new accessor.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Build the changed-function list from added definition lines plus the function enclosing each hunk (never from the `@@` text). List new headers with `--diff-filter=A`. 2. New type: grep t/ for its name; read its Note and list the invariants; check whether its size is a constexpr baked into its owner. 3. For each changed F with no t/ hit: walk callers up three levels; follow changed callees down to the first with a t/ hit; take the enclosing TEST_CASE of each hit and read it: does it call F, F's caller, or the callees by hand? List F's branches and the test that reaches each. Read the comment above F for the contract and grep t/ for the fields its barrier uses. 4. For each changed field formula, grep t/ for assignments of that field outside the diff; substitute the test's local definitions and compare. 5. For each accessor swap, read both accessors' definitions and grep body and commit messages for the new name. 6. Write a coverage statement; say what wrong behavior would still pass; keep an observed bug in a separate sentence.
skill_entry.question: Which test enters the changed code through its production entry point, and which assertion fails if that code is wrong?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A PR that changes h/ or src/ with no t/ file when it is not a new primitive, an orchestration change or a hardware-path change (20 of 48 silent PRs; negative_space 'Missing tests alone do not draw a comment'). A new type or function family added inside an existing header (tron-2693 counters, tron-2646 helpers drew nothing). A PR whose title or body says it merges, lifts or ports code from a named branch (tron-1707, 1722, 1739, 2646): the primitive only moves. Doc-only, test-only, one-line and mechanical-rename PRs (every removed/added pair differs only by the rename map). A test calling a callee directly when the diff changed only that callee. A formula hit the author shows equivalent after substituting the test's definitions (PR 1997: Wade approved 14 minutes after mcherba's last reply, without answering). An element-access respelling (`(*p)[0]` to `p->front()`). A swap a sentence explains. He asks to 'extend an existing CI suite' or for 'a unit-test', never a new file for moved code; he does not ask for a run here; he does not re-raise a bot's finding.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Orchestration: 'Coverage gap: the changed <F> is bypassed by the focused tests. The added tests call `<callee>` directly; the existing test named "<name>" invokes <steps> by hand. Please extend an existing CI suite with cases through <production entry>: <cases from F's branches>. Assert <contract>. These are missing safety-contract checks; I have not observed a <failure> in the implementation.' If the test reaches F only through a fake that ignores the arguments production emits, report under check 3. New primitive: 'Are you going to build a unit-test for `<primitive>`? Seems it should warrant one... verifying <invariant>, <invariant>, etc'. Formula: 'this should be updated in the <test files> as well'. Accessor swap: 'is this indeed the same <resource>?'
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal. A bold 'Coverage gap:' headline appears in the two PR 4128 comments (3960538961, 3960538177); the six dense PR 4128 inline comments carry no attribution header, and whether they were assistant-written is Insufficient data (wade-corpus.md:46), so cite the headline as the form of the posted finding, not as his phrasing. His own words elsewhere: 'Seems it should warrant one' (4614385493, a conversation comment); 'this should be updated ... as well... else I can do it after you merge this I guess' (2771720147); a bare question 'is this indeed the same queue?' (2737853978). Never 'nit', never blocking: he approved PR 1997 after the author's explanation and PR 2903 after the test file landed.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: full file (every TEST_CASE that hits a callee, read at HEAD), other files (t/ files the diff does not touch; the production definition of a swapped accessor), callers (production callers of the changed function, up to three levels), PR body and commit messages (for a sentence that covers a test edit). Not CI, not runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a changed path needs a test that enters it from the production side

Common setup for this check. HEAD = the commit of the review record (corpus reviews[].commit; 97de6ee02c for PR 4128 review 5144955010), never the inline comment's commit field (GitHub moves it to the later head). BASE: if `git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main` succeeds (merged PR; merge-base would return HEAD itself), use `gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefOid -q .baseRefOid`, and when that id is not in WT use the merge commit's first parent `git -C WT merge-base HEAD <mergeCommit>^1`; otherwise `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main)`.

1. New primitives. `git -C WT diff --diff-filter=A --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*'`. Skip the step when the PR title or body says it merges, lifts or ports code from a named branch. For each new header: `git -C WT show HEAD:<hdr> | grep -n -E '^ *(class|struct) [A-Za-z_]+|Note \[|\b(must|exactly once|wrap|full|empty)\b'`. A type is a candidate only when it has an advancing index or count and an array or ring sized by a constant, and at least one invariant line hit. For each candidate name: `git -C WT grep -l -w <name> HEAD -- t/`; no hit = finding. List the invariants the `Note [...]` states (ordering, wrap-around, full, empty, concurrent writers); those are the cases to ask for. Baked size: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<name>[^;]*\{[a-z_]+_size\}' HEAD -- h/` and the constant's value in h/pos/config.hpp; if baked, note that a test cannot build a small instance (the remedy wording, a constructor argument with that default, is owned by the constant-name check, id 3350173837).

2. Orchestration. Changed functions, two commands, take the union. (a) Added or rewritten definitions: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | grep -E '^\+[ \t]*(template *<[^>]*> *)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:<>,*& ]* +)?[~A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:]*\([^;]*\)[ \t]*(const)?[ \t]*(noexcept)?[ \t]*\{[ \t]*$' | grep -v -E '^\+[ \t]*(if|for|while|switch|return|else|TRON_|REQUIRE|CHECK|static_assert|catch)\b'`. (b) The function enclosing each hunk: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | awk '/^\+\+\+ b\//{f=substr($0,7)} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[+,]/); print f, a[2]}'`, then per (file, line) `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /^[ \t]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:<>,*& ]* +)?[~A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:]*\([^;]*(\)[ \t]*(const)?[ \t]*(noexcept)?[ \t]*\{[ \t]*$|,$)/ && !/^[ \t]*(if|for|while|switch|return|else|TRON_|REQUIRE|CHECK|static_assert|catch|TRACE)/ {name=$0} END{print name}'`. Drop lambdas and wrapped assertion lines by eye. Do not use the stock `@@` text: for an indented member function it prints `public:` or the enclosing struct, and an added function never appears in it.
   Per function F: `git -C WT grep -n -w F HEAD -- t/` and `git -C WT grep -n -w F HEAD -- h/ src/`. For a member name shorter than six characters, or a common verb (clear, complete, populate, reset, size), or more than 30 bare hits, grep with the access spelling instead: `git -C WT grep -n -E '(<class>::|<receiver>->|<receiver>\.)F\(' HEAD -- t/`. Record the hit count next to each name.
   Body of F: `s=$(git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E '\bF\(' | grep -E '\{ *$|noexcept *\{|\) *\{' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); e=$(git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v S=$s 'NR>=S{n+=gsub(/\{/,"{"); n-=gsub(/\}/,"}"); if(NR>S && n==0){print NR; exit}}'); git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n "${s},${e}p" | grep -o -E '\b(<changed names joined by |>)\(' | sort | uniq -c`.
   Chain: start from each production caller outside F's file; follow changed callees down until a changed function with a t/ hit appears. The outermost changed function on the chain with zero t/ hits is F; the t/-hit callee at the chain end is the "called directly" function of the finding. Caller walk: `git -C WT grep -n -w F HEAD -- h/ src/`, then each caller's callers, up to three levels; stop at the first function with a t/ hit and record it with its TEST_CASE. Branch test: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <file> | sed -n '<F hunks>' | grep -E '^[-+].*\b(if|for|while|switch)\b|\?|\.(size|empty)\(\)'`. Fire only when no caller level reaches t/ and the branch test hits; argument plumbing and one forwarding call are not a branch.
   Enclosing TEST_CASE per callee hit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<test> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /TEST_CASE\(/ {name=$0; n=NR} END{print n": "name}'`. An empty name means the hit is in a helper above the first TEST_CASE: take the helper's name with the function pattern of 2(b) and `git -C WT grep -n -w <helper> HEAD -- <test file>` for the TEST_CASEs that call it. Read each TEST_CASE: does it call F, F's production caller, or the callees by hand? List F's branches (single versus batch, reservation collision, fanout, mixed shards and layers) and the test that reaches each, or none.
   Contract: read the comment block above F (`sed -n "$((s-8)),$((s-1))p"`) and the Note it cites; list the fields F's barrier reads or writes (`grep -o -E '[a-z_]+_\.'` over F's body); `git -C WT grep -n -E '<field1>|<field2>' HEAD -- t/`. Zero hits = no assertion observes the contract.
   Author's fix at a later head FINAL: `git -C WT log --no-merges --format='%h %s' HEAD..FINAL -- t/` and `git -C WT grep -n -w -E '<F names>' FINAL -- t/`; never `git diff --stat HEAD FINAL -- t/` when a merge of main sits between (46 files on PR 4128).

3. Formula mirror. `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | grep -n -E '^[-+][^/]*\b[A-Za-z_]+(\.|->)[A-Za-z_.]+ *= *[^;=]*[%*/+-]' | grep -v -E '= *[^;]*->'`; drop a line whose target is declared on the same line. The target field is the last dotted or arrow name before ` =`; a local variable is out of scope (a test cannot mirror a local). `git -C WT grep -n -E '(\.|->)<field> *=' HEAD -- t/`. For each hit in a file not in prfiles.txt: `git -C WT show HEAD:<test> | grep -n '<local var> ='` for every variable in the test's formula, substitute, and compare with the production form. Resolve the production operand to what it counts: `git -C WT show HEAD:<src> | grep -n '<operand> ='`. Report hits that are not equivalent and hits the PR touches that still carry the old form.

4. Accessor swap. `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 't/*' | grep -n -B2 -A2 -E '^-.*(::acquire\(|pos_allocate|std::make_shared<)|^\+.*= *(dev|device)->[a-z_]+;|^[-+].*= *[A-Za-z_]+->[a-z_]+_q\b'`. A removed statement may span two lines (`DmaQueue* read_q =` then `DmaQueue::acquire(...)`): pair by the variable name on the removed `=` line with the added line that assigns the same name. Discard an added line with no removed partner (construction, not a swap), an added line whose right-hand side is a field read in arithmetic or a method chain (`dev->num_fetchers`, `dev->load_weight_q->write_next_descriptor(`), and a pair that differs only by element-access spelling (`(*p)[0]` to `p->front()`, `v.at(i)` to `v[i]`). For each kept pair: `git -C WT grep -n '<new accessor>' HEAD -- h/ src/` (definition, init site) and read the old accessor's body; decide whether both name one object. `grep -n -i '<accessor>' body.md`; `git -C WT log --format=%B BASE..HEAD | grep -n -i '<accessor>'`.

5. Report per candidate; separate the coverage statement from any observed bug and say what wrong behavior would still pass.

On PR 4128 (step 2 only; reviewed at 97de6ee02c, BASE 130ad3a652, final head 7f80aa17da): the stock `@@` list names none of the five functions; command 2(a) lists fire_gof_rodeo_batch and gof_rodeo_impl_batch, command 2(b) lists help_drain_gof (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2988) and wait_for_coop_gof (:3015). t/ hits: help_drain_gof 0, wait_for_coop_gof 0, fire_gof_rodeo_batch 0, gof_rodeo_impl_batch 0, dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers 0, xfer_gofs 2. help_drain_gof calls one changed function (fire_gof_rodeo_batch :3005) plus the unchanged gof_coop_queue_.try_dequeue, so a two-callee count does not select it; the chain does: self_attention.hpp:793 and :908 -> help_drain_gof -> fire_gof_rodeo_batch (:3039, `tasks.size() == 1` branch) -> gof_rodeo_impl_batch (:3063) -> dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers (src/tron/gof.cpp:455) -> shard::xfer_gofs, hit at t/t_phase1_integration.cpp:910 (TEST_CASE :853) and :1002 (TEST_CASE :969); xfer_gof at :1055 inside TEST_CASE "gof rodeo populates and xfers to shard" (:1017), populate by hand at :1047. Branch test on help_drain_gof: the `while (task_count < task_budget ...)` loop and `if (!gof_coop_queue_.try_dequeue(tasks[0])) return;`. Contract: comment above wait_for_coop_gof (:3010-3014, "every fire_gof_rodeo is done before the scheduler rebuilds gof_jobs"); fields gof_coop_outstanding_ and gof_coop_queue_, 0 t/ hits. Wade's comment 3960538961 sits at :3005. At 7f80aa17da: t/t_llama_unit.cpp:1020 TEST_CASE "production GOF drain handles fanout layers and reservation gaps", :1023 gof_indices{2, 3, 4}, :1099 enqueue on state.gof_coop_queue_, :1102 state.wait_for_coop_gof(), :1104 outstanding == 0, :1113-1118 dma_done per shard and GOF; wait_for_coop_gof then has 1 t/ hit, the other four still 0. 442ed0dd1a (on three comments) does not resolve in WT; 97de6ee02c resolves but is on no ref and is not an ancestor of 7f80aa17da (rebased; its subject reappears as fd9fa17f9d); 7f80aa17da is the tip of origin/mrc_dma_coalesce_02; PR 4128 is open.
On PR 2903 (step 1; 64ea13a671, BASE 09d6fce432 from baseRefOid because merge-base returns HEAD itself): new h/pos/minfifo.hpp and src/pos/minfifo.cpp; `Note [minfifo design]` at minfifo.hpp:8, `class minfifo` at :32; :16 three-state sequence number, :40 enqueue returns false when full, :44 dequeue returns nullptr when empty; `git grep -l -w minfifo 64ea13a671 -- t/` empty; size baked at b8739108f7:h/pos/device.hpp:265 `tron::minfifo inwork_queue{inwork_ring_size}` with inwork_ring_size = 2048 at h/pos/config.hpp:86; the PosDevice constructor at b8739108f7 has no ring-size argument (remedy not adopted, approved anyway). Test after the ask: t/t_minfifo.cpp (commit 340fb2f65e, 2026-06-04T03:36Z, ancestor of the approval head 2d9d0e43e2): :24 ring_size constructor (q16, q4), :53 fill to capacity, :87 wraparound, :146 4 producers x 256 exactly once, :201 per-producer order.
On PR 1997 (step 3; c502e4d61a, base branch hwattention_sync ae5f6faec0): src/pos/worker.cpp:925 `metadata.fields.ktok = ((acmd_len) % 128) + 1` (form entered in PR commit 7ca8f6fcb5; d306b805ce already carries it); :881 `acmd_len = workreq->tok_ix` in the num_acmds == 1 branch, :886-900 other branches use max_tok_per_acmd and num_tok_to_swap. t/ hits: t/t_hwattention.cpp:825 (literal 128), :1292 and t/t_hwattention_replay.cpp:549 `((num_tokens - 1) % 128) + 1`; replay :391 `num_tokens = token_idx + 1`, so the replay form is `(token_idx % 128) + 1`, equal to the production form in the single-command branch. `git diff --stat d306b805ce c502e4d61a -- t/` is empty. mcherba replied 00:34 and 00:38; Wade approved (3760151842) at 00:52, 14 minutes after the last reply, without answering.
On PR 1920 (step 4; 2d53016b44, base branch hwattention_sync b604cb860a): the PR makes the swap twice, t/t_hwattention.cpp:169-170 and :1317-1318 (`DmaQueue* read_q = dev->bypass_read_q;` with `// DmaQueue::acquire(dev, DMA_DIRECTION_RX, dmaPagesOfDesc * dmaDescPerPage);` kept as a comment), and adds one new use in t/t_hwattention_replay.cpp; the uses at :97, :521 and :680 already read dev->bypass_read_q at the base (b604cb860a:t/t_hwattention.cpp:94, :518, :673), so the base file was already mixed (three tests on bypass_read_q, two on DmaQueue::acquire at :167 and :1306). bypass_read_q declared at h/pos/device.hpp:248 (comment "Used only by some tests in t_hwattention at present", from d5c049e8ef, 2025-12-17) and acquired at src/pos/device.cpp:260-261 through `DmaQueue::acquire(this, DMA_DIRECTION_RX, ...)`; DmaQueue::acquire (src/pos/dma_queue.cpp:50-74) takes the first free queue of that direction, calls setup(ring_size), sets in_use = 1, so a second acquire returns a different queue. `git log -S bypass_read_q 2d53016b44 -- t/t_hwattention.cpp` lists b81120a08f (2026-01-27, adds the two swaps), dd2ced785b (re-spaces the comment, drops one use), and the pre-PR 6fae30e34b (2025-08-27) and c3e91be683 (2025-07-16). The one-line body "Readback of k and v transfer final portion guards." and no commit message name the swap. In gh pr diff 1920 the removed statement spans two lines, so the pair is formed by the variable name read_q.
Silent PRs the narrowed check stays off: tron-4353 (a9a9cf30a4, BASE eeb72c0348): finish_sw_plan (model.hpp:2731) has 0 t/ hits, but its caller walk reaches assemble_attention_plan at level 2 with a t/ hit (t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:182), and its own hunks (a parameter, `(void)q_batch` removed, two extra assign_page arguments at :2776-2777, one appended split_sections_by_query call at :2785) contain no branch or loop. tron-1722 (aac65930a5): "Third step of Attention on FPGA merge" (merge-from-branch rule) and h/pos/hwattention.hpp has no invariant sentence. tron-2774 (10fe891af5): fixed_string has no mutable state and no invariant sentence. tron-3756 (7206e88cc2): the field-only grep drops `dev = ...` and `device_idx = dev->idx`; `(*pos_list_devices())[0]` to `pos_list_devices()->front()` (t/t_gof_dma.cpp:47 and six sites in t/t_gof_staging_leaks.cpp) is an element-access respelling. tron-2875 (a3e710673b): extend_request::operator() is reached by sequence_prompt, a direct caller named in five t/ files. tron-2693 and tron-2646: new names inside existing headers, trigger (a) does not widen.
final.widen_delta: Checks 1 to 5 start from a test that exists and reaches the changed code; they judge the rows, the gates, the duplicates and the names. Check 14 runs one step earlier: it asks whether any test enters the changed code at all, and whether it enters through the production caller rather than a callee or hand-written steps. It adds four mechanical triggers (new stateful primitive with an invariant sentence and no t/ file, orchestration bypass on a call chain, formula mirror of a dotted field in untouched tests, unexplained accessor swap to a different named object in a test hunk) and one call-graph procedure (changed function -> t/ hits -> caller walk up three levels -> chain down to the first t/-hit callee -> enclosing TEST_CASE -> F, caller or by-hand). The changed-function list comes from added definition lines plus the function enclosing each hunk, never from the `@@` text. Two wording rules go to 'How Wade words a finding': a coverage finding says what wrong behavior would still pass, and keeps any observed bug in a separate sentence ('I have not observed a ... failure in the implementation'); the ask is 'extend an existing CI suite', not a new file. The 'Coverage gap:' headline is cited as the form of the posted PR 4128 finding, not as Wade's own phrasing (attribution Insufficient data). The baked-size remedy (constructor argument with the constant as default) is a one-line pointer here; its id 3350173837 stays with the constant-name check. The fake-boundary note (3960538177) stays with check 3; this check only cross-references it. The common setup gains two rules: HEAD is the review record's commit, and BASE for a merged PR comes from baseRefOid or the merge commit's first parent.
